Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That's all we have for you from this game. After a thrilling day 5 finish in Kolkata, this game turned out to be an anti-climax. Let's hope we don't get to witness another lopsided affair when these two meet next for the third and final Test in Delhi. Will Sri Lanka pull a rabbit out of the hat or will the plot remain the same? Join us on 2nd December, 2017 at 0930 LOCAL (0400 GMT) to catch all the action. Till then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

Indian skipper, VIRAT KOHLI, who is also the MAN OF THE MATCH, is delighted with the win. Starts by crediting the pitch which was a good one to bat on. Now credits the bowlers for doing the job when there wasn't much purchase on day 1. On previously failing to get daddy tons, he says he strives to get better and is happy to do so now. Gives a special mention to his fitness which plays an important role. On Pujara and Vijay, he states that the former is very consistent while the latter is a technically sound player who takes a lot of pride in playing Test cricket. Praises Rohit, too, for grabbing the opportunity and justifying his selection. Backs him up by saying he will certainly be in the fray in future. On his bowlers, he says first-class cricket has helped Ishant Sharma and adds Yadav and Shami haven't played as much as Bhuvneshwar Kumar has in recent times. States that all his bowlers are in good rhythm. Reckons they had asked for a pitch which has more life in it as they wanted to get some practice before flying to South Africa. Informs the track deteriorated on day 2 itself but loved the one that they got in Kolkata. Is really looking forward for the South African tour.

Sri Lankan captain, DINESH CHANDIMAL says it was a good toss to win but admits they were outplayed completely by the Indians. Reckons India is a tough team to beat and that they were really poor with their shot selections. Adds they had certain plans in mind but rues that every batter just threw it away after getting a start. Informs that Angelo Mathews is the senior player in the side and when he falls early, the rest fail to carry on. Hopes that Mathews will come back into the groove sooner for them as his side needs him. Asserts that they need to address the loss quickly. Lauds the way his bowlers bowled and expects a better batting show in the next game.
It's time for the presentation. Let's hear what the skippers have got to say.

Next up is Ishant Sharma. He reckons that since he wasn't among the wickets and the way Umesh Yadav, Mohammed Shami and Bhuvneshwar Kumar were bowling, they deserved to play ahead of him. On such tracks it is about varying the lengths, he opines. He feels good to be among the wickets now. Thanks Basu Shanker, the trainer, for pushing everybody harder in terms of fitness levels and also mentions that the skipper leads from the front in this aspect. With healthy competition in the side for the seamers, it is all about grabbing your opportunities and performing, he states.

Here's what Ashwin has to say. After the applause dies down, he says that it was a tad funny at the start of the day as some deliveries spun while the others didn't. Credits Ravindra Jadeja and Ishant Sharma for bowling well and giving the early breakthroughs. He opines that angles and heights of release of the ball matter on such tracks and that both the spinners bowled at ideal speeds. On being the quickest to get to 300 Test wickets, he says that the present players are blessed more than the others due to the technology on offer and hence it is unfair to compare players from different generations. States that he didn't bowl many carrom balls and has worked on different loading positions and release points for that. Regarding the longish lay off that he had, he reckons that the break was longer than what he had ever got, during which he played County cricket and worked on the holding role. His is still a young career and he aims to add many more and almost double the 300 wickets that he currently has. Ends saying that he is tired as spin bowling isn't just about ambling in and rolling the arm over.

Once again it was Ishant Sharma who set the tone up in the second innings while Ravindra Jadeja and Ravichandran Ashwin spun the web viciously to leave the batsmen puzzled. Umesh Yadav, too, made his presence felt on his home ground with a couple of wickets to his name. A complete team effort from India saw them EQUAL THEIR BIGGEST TEST VICTORY. Sanjay Manjrekar catches up with Ravichandran Ashwin and Ishant Sharma on the sidelines...

Two full days of play were remaining and the result was more or less certain. Sri Lanka had a monumental task ahead of them and it was disheartening to see them going down without putting up a fight. None of the batsmen apart from their skipper Chandimal (who tried his best in the first innings too) showed any resistance. Most of them were guilty of not applying themselves which didn't help their cause. Suranga Lakmal threw his bat around and strung a breezy 58-run stand with his skipper but to be honest, it was just about delaying the inevitable.

Sri Lanka lost half of the game then and there. The Indian batsmen decided to bat once but bat big. Apart from Rahul and Rahane, the rest made the most of a good batting surface. It all started with Murali Vijay (128), then Cheteshwar Pujara (143), went on to Virat Kohli (213) and ended when Rohit Sharma helped himself to an unbeaten ton (102). All of them batted with sheer authority and dictated terms to the Lankan bowlers. Finally the declaration came when Kohli felt a lead of 405 was enough.

India have dominated Sri Lanka completely to take a 1-0 lead in the series. They were put under the pump in Kolkata but it was completely a different scenario that we got to witness in Nagpur. Kohli lost an important toss but his side did everything right from thereon. You don't expect a team to be bundled out for a paltry 205 on day 1 of a Test match on a good track, do you? The Indian bowlers did that without their two strike bowlers (Shami and Kumar). Ishant Sharma on his comeback, took three while the remaining 7 wickets were taken care of by the spin twins.

OUT! Gamage is bowled! Another feather in Ashwin's cap - 300th Test wicket for him and he becomes the quickest to do so. He bowls a carrom ball, lands it around off. Gamage comes forward to defend but the ball grips and turns away and the bails are seen coming off. The umpire, Richard Kettleborough isn't sure what has happened there and hence takes it upstairs. The Indians are seen shaking hands, meanwhile. Replays show, the ball disturbs the off stick and then settles into the keeper's mitts. That's it then. INDIA WIN BY AN INNINGS AND 239 RUNS!
Oh wait! What just happened? Ashwin beats Gamage's defense, the bails have come off. The umpire isn't sure and hence it has been referred upstairs...
Tossed up on off, blocked by coming forward.
The carrom ball around middle and leg, LG looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Shortish and outside off, Lakmal once again looks to cut but misses it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
That just missed the off stump! Back of a length, tailing back in, Lakmal looks to cut but this comes back in and sneaks under his bat. This time it wasn't far away from kissing the off stump.
Sprayed miles down the leg side, poor Saha dives full stretch to his left to stop it from running away from the fence.
Shortish on middle and off, the ball seems to have skidded off the pitch. SL looks to pull but the ball sneaks under his bat and goes to the keeper.
Fuller in length and swinging back in on the pads, Lakmal is beaten for pace and wears it on the pads.
Once again the edge doesn't carry and it falls short of the man at short leg.
Just short of short leg! Floats it up around middle, Gamage looks to block it off the front foot but the ball hits the higher part of the bat and falls short of the man at FSL.
Around middle and leg, worked towards the man at leg gully.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Gamage first looks to leave but then tries to cut it away. In the end, gets beaten.
Carrom ball around middle, Gamage defends it down.
Full outside off, driven down to long off for a single.
Right into the blockhole. Spears in a yorker on the stumps, Gamage is able to dug it out.
LAHIRU GAMAGE is the last man in!

OUT! In the air... gone! It's wicket no. 99 in Tests for the local lad. Chandimal walks back in dismay. Yadav drops it on a length but the line is on the leg stump. The Lankan skipper flicks it aerially but finds Ashwin stationed at fine leg who accepts a simple catch. End of the Sri Lankan skipper's resistance. Yet another valiant knock from him but in vain. India just a wicket away from a win here.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length on middle, turned towards mid-wicket.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Leg bye! Spears it on the pads, Lakmal misses the clip and it goes off the pads towards the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Driven hard but finds the man at mid on.
The batsman gets a leading edge on that one. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Fuller in length on the stumps, driven towards the bowler.
Clears the front leg to whip it across the line but gets it off the inside edge through the gap at square leg for a couple.

NOT OUT! Nothing on the Ultra Edge! India waste a review! Ashwin slides one down leg, Lakmal leans across to clip it away but it goes towards Saha who takes it by stretching both his hands to his left. Ashwin appeals but Saha stays put. The bowler says he has heard something and that prompts Kohli to use the DRS. The front foot is fine. Ultra Edge then shows there's no bat involved.

Review time! There is a caught behind appeal against Lakmal which is referred upstairs by Kohli. Ashwin says he has heard something and his skipper wastes no time in taking the DRS. Seems like Lakmal is safe. Let's wait and watch...
Around middle, turning in, defended off the front foot.
Fuller in length and angling in, clipped towards the leg side.

Harsh Bhogle on-air has got something to say. While all the talks have been about the men who have made comebacks, Harsha says Ishant Sharma has impressed one and all. He agrees he has done the job for his side in the past but then after being in the top draw, he doesn't take time to drop down. Now that he has got into the groove, he needs to do that on a consistent basis to cement his place in the side...
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Chandimal flicks this one towards the leg side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Fuller in length and curling back in just a touch, Chandimal works it uppishly past the man at square leg. Rohit Sharma is stationed there but it goes wide of him. Pujara in the deep does the mop up work to prevent a boundary. A couple taken.
Good length delivery with a tinge of reverse on it, the Lankan skipper keeps it out safely.
The carrom ball from Ash! This one lands on off and spins away to beat the outside edge of Suranga's bat.
Gets forward and defends it with his bat and pad close to short leg.

SIX! Down the track and Lakmal goes bang! That's a quality shot and looks so good to watch. Brings up the 50-run stand off just 49 balls. Ashwin gives a truckload of flight, Lakmal dances down and bashes it powerfully over the bowler's head to add a maximum to his name.
Flatter delivery on middle, the batsman hangs back in defense.
Loops it up on the stumps, Dinesh comes down the track and nudges it wide of mid on for one.
Loopy delivery outside off, Chandimal defends it down.
Stays back and keeps it out off the front foot gently.
Fuller and tailing back in, Chandimal flicks it through mid-wicket for one.

FOUR! Inside edge and through. This one comes back in again and stays a touch low too. Chandimal just puts bat on ball and gets an inside edge which evades the leg pole and races down to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Good length ball, coming back in, Chandimal looks to work it away but squirts it off the inside edge towards short mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery on middle, blocked solidly off the back foot.
Bowls this fuller ball at 129 clicks, driven towards mid off.
UMESH YADAV to bowl from the other end!
Floated delivery around off, Lakmal prods forward in defense.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Vijay Shankar wants to enjoy himself on the field! Superb fielding effort from the young man. A bit short and outside off, slapped through the left of the backward point fielder. The sub fielder hares after it, slides to flick the ball back in play. Two taken.
This one turns in a bit, Lakmal tries to turn it away but gets it off the leading edge towards the off side.
Flatter one outside off, the batsman defends by lunging forward.

Good stop from the substitute fielder! Floated delivery outside off, Lakmal reaches out and drives it off the outer half behind point. Vijay Shankar the man there dives to his left and makes sure Lakmal remains on strike.

Welcome back for the session which might in all likelihood give us the result. India are just 2 wickets away from going 1-0 up in the series. How long can the current pair of CHANDIMAL and LAKMAL delay the defeat? RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN to begin with the ball. He is one short of 300 Test wickets. Let's see if he can get to the landmark. A slip, leg slip and a short leg in place...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Dinesh Chandimal is amidst an attacking 38-run stand with Suranga Lakmal who seems to be enjoying his time in the middle. For once, he'd imagine, he doesn't have to run in. Just stand and swish the wooden apparel in the hand and have fun - that's what he is up to. This pair is just delaying the inevitable at the moment. See you all at 1226 local time for what could be the last session or even the last hour of the game.

At home, India have an impression of grabbing a hand when you offer them a finger. And lo, the visitors did just that! All the bowlers took up the chance to get among the wickets to peg the Lankans back. Ashwin and Jadeja have struck without even looking as menacing as they could be. Umesh Yadav helped himself to his first scalp on his home ground while Ishant was rewarded for bowing in right areas. He could have got another had he managed to hang on the return catch of Lakmal. But the sport isn't about ifs and buts...

Losing seven wickets in a 135-minute play is a crime when the track is not really harsh on the batsmen. In tough situations, the experienced players need to stand up and bail the team out but today Mathews and Thirimanne were guilty of just throwing their wickets away. That gave India an opportunity to make inroads and they ended up making hay while the sun shone brightly in Nagpur. Only Chandimal has shown resistance with a fighting-yet-not-so-useful half century.

Sri Lanka on the cusp of getting bowled out but just hang on to enjoy a delicious meal! It is a sorry state for them as they failed to negotiate even a session of play when the talk was about batting out a couple of days. That's what surprises most of the cricketing world. Perennially, Sri Lanka are known to be fighters in international cricket but seeing them go down in a whimper is appalling to save the words.
Chandimal negotiates the last ball before LUNCH, DAY 4, by blocking it from the crease.

FOUR! Dinesh Chandimal gets to his 15th Test fifty! On a length outside off, he guides it past backward point by opening the face of the bat to get to the mark. Twin fifties for him in this game but it's a little too late. He now holds the record of becoming the third Lankan captain to score two fifty-plus scores in the same Test against India.
Cheeky Russel Arnold! After that dropped catch, he wonders what hampered Ishant there. Adds that now the tall lanky pacer doesn't have his long manes that come in the way to block his vision.
Back of a length outside off, hit through cover for a single.

FOUR! Forget about all the live-by-the-sword sayings for a while. Lakmal's having fun wielding his willow. Ishant angles it into the batsman on a length. Lakmal looks to flick it but gets a leading edge. The ball flies over covers and rolls away to the fence.

Dropped! Play has been extended by 15 minutes for India to pick wickets and wrap the match up. The chance comes around and goes abegging now. Fuller delivery around middle, Lakmal expecting a short one hangs on the back foot. Ends up pushing it back to the bowler. The tall pacer gets down well but fails to cling on. Falls flat on the ground in disappointment.
On a length around off, Lakmal stays in the crease and blocks it.
ISHANT SHARMA back on.

FOUR! Chandimal takes the spinner on and connects. This is a leg break from Ashwin, not sure Chandimal picked it up. Gets down and plays the slog sweep with what he supposes is with the spin. Gets a top edge that lands just short of going the distance. Gets a boundary that takes him to 49!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around off, pushed towards point.
Dinesh lunges forward and defends it with a straight bat.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and connects. They pick up a single.
Flatter around off, Lakmal goes back to block.
FOUR! Loopy delivery on the stumps, Lakmal comes down the track and hits it over mid on. Ishant Sharma runs backwards but has no chance of getting to it and stopping the boundary.
Lakmal goes back and punches it through cover-point. Pujara chases it down and fumbles a bit as he tries to retrieve the ball. Results in a brace.
Lakmal keeps it out with a straight bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. One run added to the total. A single taken.
Around off and middle, turned towards mid-wicket.
Before this delivery, Kohli and Ashwin had a chat about something. Not sure what it was about but Ashwin bowls a leg break here. Ends up being a full toss that is hit back towards the bowler.
Lakmal hits it in the air towards deep mid-wicket. One run is all he gets.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. Good running between the wickets to pick up three runs.
Dinesh lunges forward and blocks it watchfully.
Flatter outside off, Lakmal goes back to block but gets it off the outer half past slip for a run.
Outside off, eased through covers for a brace.
Turned through mid-wicket for a run. Ashwin won't mind this as he will bowl to Suranga in the next over.
Lakmal has punched the ball off the backfoot. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Lunges forward and buries it onto the ground.
Lunch is extended by 15 minutes. If another one falls, it'll be extended by half an hour.
FOUR! That is one way to play Jadeja. Seeing this floated delivery around off, Lakmal frees his arms and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Eased towards mid off.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Chandimal sweeps it through square leg for a brace.
Flicked aerially through mid-wicket for a run.
SURANGA LAKMAL walks in at number 10 for Sri Lanka.

OUT! Oh dear! Sri Lankans are going on a bit too fast for anybody's liking here. Ashwin lands it around middle and leg, Herath prods forward in defense. But the extra bounce on this one means that the ball hits his gloves and lobs to Rahane at slip. He takes it and the Indians begin to celebrate. The veteran starts to walk off. Ashwin is now one shy of 300 Test scalps.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
RANGANA HERATH is the next man walking in with the bat for the visitors.

OUT! Yes it is wicket no. 500 in international cricket for Ravichandran Ashwin! He bowls it flatter and quicker around off and middle, it just spins in a touch. Perera misses the attempted flick shot. The Indians go up in unison in appealing for LBW, which the umpire upholds after thinking. Perera isn't convinced and has a chat with Chandimal before opting for DRS. Replays show that the ball would go on to clip the leg stump. Hence the on-field call stays. The visitors don't lose the review though. This is Ashwin's 50th wicket in this calendar year.
Is it no. 500 for Ashwin? Given on-field as an LBW decision but Perera, after a chat with his skipper, chooses to review the same.
DC keeps it out by pushing it towards mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Chandimal lunges forward and blocks.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, cut away.
RAVINDRA JADEJA back into the attack.
Chandimal flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Even after watching a wicket fall in this over due to attacking, Chandimal doesn't hold back. Uses his feet to get to the pitch of the ball and hits it over mid on. The ball goes to the fence on one bounce.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
DILRUWAN PERERA makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! This was always coming with the way Dasun Shanaka was playing. You live by the sword and die by it goes the saying and seldom is it proved wrong. Shanaka was hell-bent on attacking the spinner and pays the price for doing so on this occasion. Ashwin tosses it around off, Shanaka comes down to belt it out of Nagpur. But he ends up getting more height than distance on it. KL Rahul has his eyes on the ball as he runs back from mid on and manages to hold to that. Not easy are these skiers but he doesn't fluff it. The tourists are crumbling in a hurry here. Ashwin adds one to his wickets column.
Chandimal pushes it towards mid off and crosses over to the other end.
Flicked towards short leg from the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. One run added to the total.
Chandimal has attempted to put bat on ball, but fails.
Around off, blocked solidly.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Edgy but Sri Lanka won't mind these. Length delivery just outside off, Chandimal gets squared up in defense. Gets an outside edge that lands short of the fielder at second slip and races away to the fence.
FOUR! Chandimal has used the angle of the ball well. Slanted on the pads, the Sri Lankan skipper flicks it away through backward square leg for a boundary.

SIX! And another one! Same area, same result. A maximum. Floated around off, Shanaka goes big over deep mid-wicket. This time it comfortably clears the fielder stationed in that region. 16 runs off this one.
DS has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
SIX! There goes Shanaka again. Gets the desired result too. Ashwin tosses it around off, Dasun gets to the pitch of the ball and hits it all the way over deep mid-wicket.
Dasun looks to turn it away with the spin but ends up getting a leading edge that lands safely towards covers.

FOUR! Well, well! Facing the spinner is tough, ehh? Shanaka doesn't think so. He uses his feet to get down and hits it over mid-wicket. There is a man back-tracking but he fails to get there. A boundary results.
Flatter around off, Shanaka looks to play the sweep but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Dasun plays the pull shot. They pick up a single. Gets off the mark with this.
DASUN SHANAKA makes his way out at the fall of the 5th Lankan wicket. He has had a pretty ordinary series with the bat so far. Rectification time?

OUT! Kohli fumbles but doesn't let the chance go down. Dickwella, before the start of play today, spoke of playing as per the situation. He did to a certain extent but the pitch and the delivery have got the better of him here. Ishant lands it on a length around off, the ball moves away just a bit after pitching. Dickwella had to play at that and hangs his bat out. There is some extra bounce there which means that the ball takes the edge and goes to Virat at second slip who fumbles but takes it on the second attempt. Sri Lanka are withering away too soon. India 5 wickets away from a win.
Again ND finds mid on with the flick.
Length delivery outside off, Chandimal gets it through point for a single.
Gets a run this time as he plays it through point.
Sharma steams in from round the wicket and serves it on a length around off. Niroshan stays in the crease and pushes it towards mid on.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Chandimal sweeps it to the man in front of square on the leg side.

Turn and bounce! Ashwin tosses this outside off, Chandimal goes back to keep it out. The ball spins in sharply to beat him all ends up on the inner side. Saha behind gets some glove to that which makes the ball go up. The close-in fielder takes it and a stifled appeal follows. This should keep the spinners interested.
Around off, Dinesh prods forward in defense.
Chandimal defends it from within the crease.
Floated around off, Dickwella gets down and sweeps it through backward square leg for a run.
Double change. RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN is brought in to bowl. Has the presence of a southpaw mooted this move? Perhaps.
DC defends it from within the crease.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.

Fair point. As Wriddhiman Saha dived full stretch to his left, Sanjay Manjrekar on-air says that this where the diminutive keeper is better than MS Dhoni. Agreed. The latter is known more for his swift hands and clean work than for his diving and throwing-his-body-around abilities.
Sharma strays down the leg side but Chandimal misses the flick. The keeper dives to his left to collect that and prevent runs.

Wow! Look at the purchase that Ishant has got here. The lanky pacer lands it on a length around off and middle, Chandimal looks to flick it away. There is some extra bounce on that which means that the ball hits him high on the back part of the bat and hits him on his right bicep. The ball rolls towards the slip cordon. Would be painful for Dinesh.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

This, this is what I meant a couple of balls ago. These are harmless deliveries outside off that can well be left alone. Yet Chandimal has a slash at that but misses. Wasn't far away from getting the outer edge.
ISHANT SHARMA to run in with the ball now. With Jadeja striking from one end, Kohli wants to create pressure from the other end too.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Chandimal rotates strike by flicking it through mid-wicket. He is on 18 off 20 balls. Yet again he has got himself going and needn't do anything weird to get out. Sri Lanka still 333 runs behind.
Served outside off, left alone by the Lankan skipper.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
There's the flatter and quicker one that Jaddu bowls. At 90 kph! Chandimal goes back and hurriedly chops it towards point.
Dickwella flicks this through square leg for a single.
This ball is pushed towards covers.
Dinesh gets forward and blocks it solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Chandimal defends this towards point.
Dickwella gets going with a punch off the back foot through covers.

Ishant Sharma confronted by a rocket! Chandimal taps this length delivery in front of covers and sets off for a run. Jadeja there, gets ahead and hurls a wild throw at the bowler's end. Sharma backing up stops it cleanly but loses balance due to the force of the throw. A run results.

Floated outside off, Dickwella goes for the sweep again but misses. Wears it on the pad again to draw India's appeal. Umpire shakes his head in negation. Kohli ponders about the review but decides against it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
ND keeps it out watchfully from the crease.
Dickwella looks to sweep this away but misses and gets rapped on the front pad. A stifled appeal follows but dies down on its own. The impact was well outside off.
NIROSHAN DICKWELLA is the next man in. The young lad has too much potential to deliver but is found guilty of throwing it away at the same time.

OUT! Irresponsible shot from a senior player, says Simon Doull on-air! Pretty much sums up the scenario. Mathews and Chandimal are the experienced players in the side and everyone would look up to them to help their side to safety. But here is the former doing something he could have avoided. Jadeja tosses this outside off, invites Angelo to drive. The Lankan batsman falls into the bait and plays it aerially straight to Rohit Sharma at mid off, who gleefully accepts the offering. Another one bites the dust, India 6 wickets away from a win.
Flatter around off, Mathews stays back watchfully keeps it out.

Drinks are on the field. What an hour it turned out to be for the Indians. They wasted no time in drawing first blood this morning. They were helped by some poor shot selections. Jadeja is getting good amount of purchase, Yadav is getting the ball to reverse and one would feel the batting will only get difficult now. What do we have in store next? Can Sri Lanka survive till lunch?

FOUR! Umesh Yadav is bowling too straight. I understand he is searching for the reverse swing but at the same time you need to get your line right. It's on the pads, Chandimal shuffles across and flicks it through backward square leg for a boundary to end the over.

Direct hit and Chandiaml would have been a goner! Really poor call from Mathews, this! He punches this length ball towards Rahul at cover-point and sets off. The Indian opener attacks the ball and has a shy the striker's end but misses. Replays show Chandimal would have been well short had that it. Risky!
Yadav is hiding the ball. This is because he is getting the ball to reverse...
Fuller in length, just outside off, AM keeps his willow inside the line and lets it past.
Short of a length outside off, Chandimal looks to slash at it. Gets a bottom edge which rolls towards point and a single is picked up.
Back of a length outside off, punched in the gap through cover-point for one.
Shortish in length and bowled outside off, Mathews looks to glide it down to third man. He gets an edge which lands well short of Rahane at gully.
Tossed up on the pads, worked through backward square leg for a single.
An arm ball on the stumps, safely kept out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Darted on the pads, clipped behind square on the leg side for one.

Extra bounce! Jadeja shortens his length and extracts some bounce, Chandimal initially comes forward but seeing the length he goes back. The ball hits the higher portion of the bat and dies down on the pitch.
Tossed up outside off, blocked by coming forward.
Umesh looks for some reverse swing, goes full but it's too straight. Nudged fine down the leg side for a single.
Sprayed on the pads, flicked behind square on the leg side for a single.
AM defends it from within the crease.
Fuller in length and stays a bit low too. Dinesh pushes it towards cover and takes a single.
Touch fuller on off, aiming in on off, pushed towards mid off.

FOUR! Edged but safe! Shortish of a length delivery outside off, Chandimal throws his hands at it. Gets it off the outside edge but luckily it flies safely behind square on the off side for a boundary. A streaky one.
Flatter and shorter in length on middle, punched back to the bowler.
Drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Ripper from Jadeja! He drags his length back, bowls it on the shorter side and gets it to turn away. Mathews plays for the original line and that nearly costs him.
Tossed up outside off, driven into the cover region.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted delivery outside off, defended into the ground.

FOUR! Chandimal is off the mark! Fuller and curling back in on middle, Chandimal flicks it uppishly through square leg. Gets away with that one and picks up a boundary to his name. Umesh wouldn't mind this. Excellent over from the pacer.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
DINESH CHANDIMAL steps out to bat. He was amongst runs in the first innings before throwing it away. Can he bail his side out of trouble?

OUT! Straight to Jadeja! That's a poor shot to be honest. Umesh Yadav picks up his first wicket of the Test match. He serves a full ball, sprayed wider outside off. Thirimanne could have left that alone but for some reason he tries to go after it. Looks to drive it away from the body but ends up slicing it straight to Jadeja at backward point who accepts a dolly. There's a reason Lahiru Thirimanne has the WORST batting average amongst top 6 Lankan batsmen in Tests with a minimum of 1000 runs (22.63). Sri Lanka slip further.
Fuller and aiming in on the stumps, Thirimanne brings his bat down at the angle and manages to jam it out towards mid-wicket.
Good length on off, defended by getting across a touch.
Short of a length delivery, just outside off, Thirimanne gets squared up a touch as the ball goes off the edge towards gully.

SIX! What a way to get off the mark! This should get him going. Tossed up outside off, Mathews gets down and fetches it from outside off. He has got so much power behind the shot that it easily sails over the long on fence for a biggie all way.
Tossed up outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne leans ahead and with an open face bat guides it past Rahane at first slip. The fielder gives it a chase and does well to prevent a boundary. Three runs taken.
Comes down the track and drives it towards the mid on fielder.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Drifting away outside off, Thirimanne gets forward to defend but gets it off the edge past Rahane at first slip.
Tossed up outside off, Lahiru prods forward in defense.
Fuller and tailing back in a touch, Mathews looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. He nearly falls over. No real appeal as it was going down leg.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good ball! On a length and served away outside off, Mathews comes forward to defend but there is a bit of movement inward that gets the better of Angelo here which beats him.
Length ball on off, tapped in front of cover for a quick single.
Length delivery but once again on the pads, clipped behind square on the leg side for a brace.
Shortish in length on middle and leg, wristed towards short mid-wicket.
UMESH YADAV is brought into the attack for the first time in this innings. He was the only bowler who went wicketless in the first innings for India. Can he redeem himself on his home ground?
An arm ball on middle and off, Mathews leans ahead and defends it watchfully.
Fuller and bowled outside off, Mathews presses forward and defends it gently into the ground.
Drifting in around off, blocked off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gets forward and kills it into the ground.
Flighted outside off, driven towards cover for a single.
Stands back and pushes it with an angled bat towards point.
Back of a length outside off, Mathews comes forward to defend but the ball holds it line and he gets beaten.

Manjrekar on air has got something to say for Kohli here. He likes his captaincy. Adds Kohli doesn't like to attack too much, enjoys playing the waiting game. This can work at home as it guarantees him a wicket here but he needs to think something when he goes overseas. He is keen to see him how he fares outside home...
Length delivery on middle, clipped towards Rohit at short leg who half-stops but the batsmen take a single.
Outside off, on a length, left alone.
Good length delivery on middle, defended down.
Short and angling in on the body, turned towards mid-wicket.
Wicket maiden! Mathews takes a stride forward and blocks it down. A successful first over from Jadeja.
Drifts one around off, Mathews is well forward and defends it down.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards cover.
ANGELO MATHEWS is the new man in!

OUT! India have struck early this morning! The bowling change has done the trick for Kohli but credit to Vijay for being alert here. Jadeja lands it around middle, it spins back in. Karunaratne isn't to the pitch of the ball but still goes on with the clip. Gets it off the inner half and it goes straight to forward short leg who crouches and takes it. In fact, it hits him on the stomach but he manages to cling onto that one. These kind of catches are never easy. Murali Vijay is delighted as he lofts his arms and sprints in joy. A big wicket for India as Karunaratne is the one in form of late. Sri Lanka trail by 371 runs!
Fuller on middle, worked towards mid-wicket.
RAVINDRA JADEJA is brought to roll his arm over. He bowled only one over yesterday and is called early into the attack today. A slip, leg slip and bat-pad for him.
Lovely delivery and nearly gets Ishant a wicket! Length delivery on off, it holds its line as well. Thirimanne comes forward to defend but is beaten all ends up. Saha fails to collect it cleanly.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Stands tall and opens the face of the bat to dab it towards backward point.
Goes around the wicket and hits it on a length on off, Thirimanne is right behind the line to defend it down.
Slanted outside off, left alone.

Ishant is steaming in here! He bangs in a short ball on middle, at 141 kmph. Thirimanne wasn't expecting this as he is late in bringing his bat to the ball. Gets it off the inner half towards square leg.
Drifting it around middle and off, LT drives it past the cover-point fielder for a single.
Slower through the air, landed outside off, Lahiru defends it down with soft hands.
Straighter one from Ashwin, Thirimanne is well forward to keep it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good running! Fuller on middle, Karunaratne drives it towards mid on and takes Rahul on. The Indian opener is quick to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses it. A single taken.
Flatter one outside off, pushed towards point for a quick single.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side.

Edged but falls just short! This is really good bowling from Ishant! He slants it across Karunaratne, who without any foot movement tries to fiddle with it. Gets a nick but luckily for him it lands just short of Pujara at first slip. He got cautious after the previous delivery and that is why he played this one with soft hands.
Extra bounce from a full length for the tall lad! Karunaratne comes forward to deal with this but since Ishant hit the deck hard he got the extra bounce and it hits the shoulder of the bat.

The commentators on air analyze about Ashwin here. They have shown clips of the wickets that he has picked in the first innings. All the 4 batters tried to play for the turn but ended up gifting their wickets to the straighter ones. Shows they played Ashwin in their minds rather than in reality.
Fuller delivery on off, Dimuth doesn't offer any shot.
Karunaratne gets across to this length delivery and keeps it out.
Shortish length delivery on off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, driven towards cover.
That's spun a long way! Nothing Thirimanne could do about it. Tossed up outside off, Lahiru lunges forward to defend but the ball turns away sharply and beats the outside edge by a whisker.

FOUR! Ahh... shot! Thirimanne doesn't care how many times Ashwin has dismissed him. He sees the flight this time and decides to cash in on it. Shimmies down a touch, gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over mid off. Nearly goes the distance. Well played!
Loops it up outside off, blocked off the front foot. Ashwin has dismissed Thirimanne on 12 occasions across formats. Is he his bunny?
Quicker one around middle and leg, Thirimanne plays for the trajectory but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball goes past the man at short leg.
Touch fuller and slanted outside off, defended off the front foot towards mid off.
Dabbed towards Rahane at gully. These angled bat shots can always be dangerous especially in the morning when the ball is expected to move around. Should be careful here, Dimuth.
Back of a length delivery on the stumps, defended nicely off the back foot.
Slants it away on a length outside off, just a deft touch past Rahane at gully. Jadeja from backward point gives it a chase and keeps them down to a couple.
Back of a length delivery on middle, much better this time. Defended with a straight bat.

FOUR! Not an ideal way to start the day! But Karunaratne won't mind it at all! Sharma comes from over the wicket and drops it on a length on the pads. Dimuth moves inside the line and clips it fine down the leg side for a boundary. First one of the day for the visitors.
Pace from the other end. ISHANT SHARMA to steam in. Two slips and a gully place...
Floats it up on the stumps, blocked watchfully. A maiden to start off with for Ashwin.
Makes a bit of room and pushes it towards mid off.
Loopy ball outside off, driven towards Kohli at short cover. The Indian skipper is casual in his attempt and lets the ball through. Still they don't risk taking a single.
Silly point moves out, short leg in place now...
Quicker one around middle and off, defended gently off the front foot.
Drifting in around middle and leg, Lahiru tries clipping it away but the ball goes off the pads.
From around the wicket, Ashwin floats it up outside off, Thirimanne leans ahead and defends it solidly back to the bowler.

The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the Indians. The overnight batsmen DIMUTH KARUNARATNE and LAHIRU THIRIMANNE walk out to resume the battle. The hosts begin with RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN first up this morning. Two slips and a silly point in place...

Russel Arnold interviews Niroshan Dickwella. The Lankan wicketkeeper says that they are ready for today. Reckons that although they've been on the field for a couple of days, they are prepared mentally to bat out two days. States that his side is planning to take it session by session. Insists there are plans for the team as well as for individuals. Goes on to say that the batsmen can't play their normal game as they have to bat out time. About his style of play, he feels that sometimes he can go in the middle and play his natural game but mostly he adjusts according to the situations. With experienced guys like Dinesh Chandimal and Angelo Mathews in the side and also with Dimuth Karunaratne, their in-form batsman at the crease, his job is more to support them he feels. Ends opining that although there was a bit of spin towards the end of yesterday, it is still a good track for batting.

PITCH REPORT - Sunil Gavasakar starts by saying Sri Lanka need to play for survival. Agrees that they will be low on confidence but they have to come out with a positive mindset. Opines the visitors should go for runs but at the same time need to be patient. Simon Doull adds they need not play rash shots just like they did in the first innings. Reckons this pitch has flattened out completely and the way the Indians batted is a proof of that. All the Lankans need to do is to put up a fight as the pitch doesn't have too many demons on it.

India will be flying high at the moment. They displayed a tremendous batting show to get a lead 405 runs which just shows how impeccable this side has become over the last few years. They will be confident of taking a 1-0 lead but the question is will they be able to wrap things up today or will they get a taste of their own medicine? The wicket isn't that difficult to bat on, it's all about mental strength. The hosts would know that they need to consistently land the ball in the right areas to reap dividends. Meanwhile, Simon Doull is alongside Sunil Gavaskar for the pitch report...

Greetings one and all! It's the first day of the week and many regard this as the 'Monday Blues.' If this is anything to go by, Sri Lanka will be the one facing it today. Two full days to go and to bat out against a quality spin attack isn't easy by any means. Just a reminder, they are already one wicket down and the pressure lies firmly on them. Agreed, they have a few experienced batsmen in their ranks but who will put up a hand and bail them out or at least stand there and show some resistance?
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then! 2 days to go and only one team can win from here, unless Sri Lanka pull off something miraculous. They were made to toil hard for over two days and now it's up to their batsmen to save them from the blushes. They trail by a mammoth 384 and it would be interesting to see if they can put up a good fight. Considering their recent batting performances, they must already be dreading with the thought of tomorrow. They have no choice of running away from it. Join us at 0930 LOCAL TIME (0400 GMT) to see if this turns out to be the last day of the match. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

ROHIT SHARMA is up for a chat. Let's see what he has got to say. Smiles and says that his side was in a good position when he walked out to bat but the ball had started to take some turn. Adds the cherry was soft and the idea was to just rotate strike. States he was nervous as it has been roughly over 500 days he last played a Test match. Is happy that he got to bat when the team wasn't under pressure and made the most of the opportunity given to him. On being out of the side for a while, he feels he missed out on something very important as he was injured when India played 13 Tests at home last year. Is disappointed about the fact that his debut got delayed by three years as in 2010 when he was drafted into the side, injuries hampered him.

The moment Sharma reached the milestone, his side declared and took a lead of a massive 405 runs over the visitors. They came out to bowl for 9 overs and guess what? They snaffled a wicket too. Ishant Sharma got one to nip back in to send Samarawickrama back and dent the Lankans further. Ashwin bowled tight lines and it seems that a completely different surface is given to the hosts.

What a day for India! Their domination continues as they walk back to the dressing room with heads held high. They batted with sheer authority and denied Sri Lanka any semblance of joy for most part of the day. Pujara couldn't swell his overnight score to much but it was a day the Indian skipper ain't forgetting any sooner. He stroked a splendid double ton alongside Rohit Sharma who on his comeback, registered a ton of his own.
This stays really low! Fuller and fired on off, Dimuth Karunaratne does well to keep it out but gets it off the outer half towards point. STUMPS ON DAY 3!

Excellent stop from Pujara! Kohli likes it too. Loopy ball outside off, Karunaratne comes down the track and drives it wide of mid on. Seemed to go to a boundary but Pujara there dives full length to his left and stops it. He was outstanding on the field in the first innings as well.
Gets across and flicks it towards the leg side.
Flatter one middle, defended watchfully.
Gets forward and buries it into the ground.
Starts off from around the wicket and bowls it on middle, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
RAVINDRA JADEJA to bowl the last over of the day. Can he pick up a wicket?
Loopy delivery outside off, driven towards cover.
Floats it up around off, blocked into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Quicker one on leg, the batsman goes back to flick but the ball goes off the pads towards fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Flatter delivery around middle and off, Dimuth goes back and defends.
Floated delivery outside off, Karunaratne leans forward and blocks it out.
Back of a length delivery on middle, it rises a touch as LT looks to defend it off the front foot. The ball hits the higher part of the bat.
Bangs in a short delivery on middle and leg, Thirimanne quickly ducks under it.
Fuller on the stumps, driven towards the mid on fielder.
Good length delivery, close to the off stump line, defended by getting right behind the line.
Shortish outside off, tapped towards point.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Thirimanne gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Drifting in on off, defended by lunging forward. A maiden from Ashwin!
DK has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted delivery outside off, jammed out comfortably.
That's spun! Ashwin drops it outside off, it hits some of the cracks and turns away towards first slip. Dimuth is surprised seeing that. Rahane at first slip likes it.
Flattish on the stumps, Karunaratne digs it out.
Floats it up around middle and off, blocked by coming forward.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Thirimanne blocks it out.
Good length outside off, no shot offered.
Goes around the wicket does Ishant and serves a length delivery around the hips. Dimuth moves across a bit and clips it fine down the leg side for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Hits the length on middle, Karunaratne stays right behind the line and defends.
Outside off, DK shoulders his arms.
Floated delivery outside off, Lahiru digs it out.
Flatter one around middle, Thirimanne hangs back in defense.
Loops it up outside off, LT prods forward to keep it out.
Floats it up on a shorter length outside off, pushed off the back foot towards point.
Goes back and flicks it straight to the short leg fielder.
Loopy delivery outside off, Thirimanne leans forward and blocks it out.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Fuller on the stumps, defended towards short mid-wicket.
Short mid-wicket in place. He removes one man from the slips but why? The ball is new and edges can fly in the cordon anytime...
FOUR! Fuller and coming back in a bit, Karunaratne flicks it but the bat turns in his hands. Still gets it wide of the man at mid on and picks up a boundary.
Stays behind the line and blocks it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Good length outside off, pushed towards cover for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
On middle and leg, driven towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Shot! Loopy delivery outside off, Karunaratne dills it through mid off and gets going.

Another appeal, this time for bat-pad! Not given! Loopy ball around middle and leg, Dimuth lunges forward to defend but gets it off something towards short leg. They appeal once more but Kettleborough stays put. Kohli once again thinks about the review but decides against it after the lack of support from his mates. Replays show it went off the pads.

An appeal straightaway! Floats it up from around the wicket and lands it around middle. Karunaratne comes forward to defend but gets hit on the pads. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Kohli and his bowler have a chat but then they decide against it. Replays show there was a thick inside edge.
RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN to share the new cherry from the other end. Ideal call, as two lefties are out there.

FOUR! Edged and through! Back of a length delivery, angling away from the southpaw, Thirimanne looks to clip it away but gets a leading edge as the ball flies safely through the gully region for a boundary. 8 from the over and a wicket too! Perfect start for India.
FOUR! Sri Lanka are away! Ishant sprays one down the leg side, Lahiru moves inside the line and gets enough bat to send it across the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle and off, LT covers the line and defends.
A bit too wide this time outside off, left alone by Thirimanne.
LAHIRU THIRIMANNE walks in next at no. 3, replacing Samarawickrama. Three slips and a gully in place...

OUT! Castled! An error in judgement? Maybe! Ishant Sharma drops it on a length outside off and this one nips back in after pitching. Samarawickrama doesn't account for the inward movement. Tries to shoulder his arms as the ball curls back in and goes on to hit the stumps. He can't believe what just happened and slowly walks off. Smiles all around in the Indian camp. Sri Lanka 1 down with no runs on the board. Actually, you can't blame Sadeera completely here. In the first innings, the ball was pitched exactly on the same line and length and Sadeera edged that due to the away movement but this time he tries to leave it. Much to his dismay this one nips back in and that proves fatal.

Ishant Sharma starts off from over the wicket and hurls a length delivery a bit wide outside off, Sadeera Samarawickrama you need not play at those. He looks to drive it away from the body and nearly pays the price for the umpteenth no. of time. A good take from Saha as he dives full length to his right to collect it.
